summary: Dewei Zhang works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Nyima, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard University in 1926 and held posts at the University of Calcutta, Gujarat University, Harvard University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1925) and held positions at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.
Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone, and held posts at the Open University (~2008) and the University of Chester (2019).
Di Jiang works in linguistics, computational linguistics, and Tibetology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo specializes in sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, and previously studied under James Steele.

Diana L. Eck (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held professorial appointments at Harvard University from circa 1976 to 2024.

Diana Lange (born 1973) works in Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE, holding posts at Humboldt, Leipzig, Zurich, Museum am Rothenbaum, Max Planck Institute, and the University of Hamburg.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (completed by 1977). As attested in 2005, she held posts as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Myōsei Tatsuguchi and William M. Bodiford at UCLA (PhD 2010), later holding posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda specialized in Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA at Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger, later holding posts at Heidelberg, the University of Cologne (1990–2006), and visiting positions at Munich, FU Berlin, Pondicherry, and PMIST.

Dieter George (1935–1985) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He held a post at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1972–1985) and served as editor for the Verzeichnis der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (~1972–1985).

Dieter Gunkel (born 1981) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at UCLA (~2005–2010) and held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA (2024).
